packages
```{r}
library(DECIPHER)
library(dada2)
library(ShortRead)
library(Biostrings)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ShortRead)
library(purrr)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
```

set seed of reproducability
```{r}
set.seed(106)
```

filenames should be the same for all forward and reverse files, such as:

*samplename*_R1_001.fastq.gz         for forward reads 
*samplename*_R2_001.fastq.gz         for reverse reads

define directory path of sequences to be processed
```{r}
path <- "" ### <- */fastq
```

create a vector of file names, one for the forward reads and one for the reverse. for illumina data, the sample name is usually everything before the first underscore
```{r}
# filter and store only fastq.gz files
fwd_files <- sort(list.files(
  path,
  pattern = "_R1_001\\.fastq\\.gz$",
  full.names = TRUE
))

rev_files <- sort(list.files(
  path,
  pattern = "_R2_001\\.fastq\\.gz$",
  full.names = TRUE
))
```

it is also useful to create a vector of just sample names
```{r}
samples = str_extract(basename(fwd_files), "^[^_]+")
names(fwd_files) <- samples
names(rev_files) <- samples
```

select primers based on target amplicon. include reverse compliement in case the amplicon sequence is shorter than read length. NOTE: for beta-tubulin isotype-1, four primer pairs are used
```{r}
# fw primers
fwd_primer <- c(
  "ACGCACTCTTTGGGAGGAGG",
  "TACGCATTCTCTTGGAGGAGG",
  "CGCATTCWCTTGGAGGAGG",
  "CGCATTCYTTGGGAGGAGG"
)
# rv primers
rev_primer <- c(
  "TGTGAGTTTTAGTGTGCGGAAG",
  "TGTGAGCTTCAATGTGCGGAA",
  "GTGAGYTTCAAWGTGCGGAAG",
  "GTGAGTTTYAAGGTGCGGAAG"
)

fwd_primer_rev <- as.character(reverseComplement(DNAStringSet(fwd_primer)))
rev_primer_rev <- as.character(reverseComplement(DNAStringSet(rev_primer)))
```

count number of reads in which each primer is found
```{r}
primer_hits <- function(primer, reads) {
    nhits <- vcountPattern(primer, sread(reads), fixed = FALSE)
    sum(nhits > 0)
}

fwd_reads <- readFastq(fwd_files[[1]])
rev_reads <- readFastq(rev_files[[1]])

# fw primer in fwd reads
fw_count <- sapply(fwd_primer, primer_hits, reads = fwd_reads)
# fe primer in rev reads
fw_rc_count <- sapply(fwd_primer_rev, primer_hits, reads = rev_reads)
# rv primer in rev reads
rv_count <- sapply(rev_primer, primer_hits, reads = rev_reads)
# rv primer in fwd reads
rv_rc_count <- sapply(rev_primer_rev, primer_hits, reads = fwd_reads)

# generate table
primer_table <- data.frame(
  primer_type = rep(c("FW", "FW_rc", "RV", "RV_rc"), each = length(fwd_primer)),
  primer = c(fwd_primer, fwd_primer_rev, rev_primer, rev_primer_rev),
  count = c(fw_count, fw_rc_count, rv_count, rv_rc_count)
)
```

install cutadapt using conda and run in RStudio using the 'system2' command. the first parameter to system2 is the program to run and the second is a character vector of arguments and their values
```{r}
cutadapt <- path.expand("/opt/miniconda3/envs/cutadapt_env/bin/cutadapt")
# check version
system2(cutadapt, args = "--version")
# 5.2
```

create output filenames for the cut files, and define the parameters we are going to give the cutadapt command. the critical parameters are the primers, and they need to be in the right orientation, i.e. the fw primer should have been matching the forward-reads in its forward orientation, and the RV primer should have been matching the reverse-reads in its forward orientation. 

briefly:
-g: sequence to trim off the 5’ end of the forward read (the forward primer)
-a: sequence to trim off the 3’ end of the forward read (the reverse complemented reverse primer)
-G: sequence to trim off the 5’ end of the reverse read (the reverse primer)
-A: sequence to trim off the 3’ end of the reverse read (the reverse complemented forward primer)

in addition, add:
-m 50: to get rid of very short or low-quality reads
--max-n 1: to get rid of reads that have any N’s in them (ambiguous base calls)
-n 2: so that cutadapt will remove multiple primer hits if there happens to be read-through
--discard-untrimmed: is also added so only reads that contain a primer will be kept ensuring we keep only valid amplicons
-q 15: will trim off low quality bases from the 3’ end

this small amount of trimming can remove the need for truncating the reads later on but this is something that may vary from run to run

create an output directory to store the cut files
```{r}
cut_dir <- file.path(path, "cutadapt_beta_tubulin_isotype-1")
if (!dir.exists(cut_dir)) dir.create(cut_dir)

fwd_cut <- file.path(cut_dir, basename(fwd_files))
rev_cut <- file.path(cut_dir, basename(rev_files))

names(fwd_cut) <- samples
names(rev_cut) <- samples
```

it's good practice to keep some log files so create some file names that we can use for those 
```{r}
cut_logs <- path.expand(file.path(cut_dir, paste0(samples, ".log")))

cutadapt_args <- c(
  "-a", rev_primer_rev,
  "-A", fwd_primer_rev,
  "-n", 2,
  "--discard-untrimmed"
)

fwd_args <- unlist(lapply(fwd_primer, function(p) c("-g", p)))
rev_args <- unlist(lapply(rev_primer, function(p) c("-G", p)))
cutadapt_extra <- c(
  "-n", 
  "2",
  "--discard-untrimmed",
  "-m", 
  "50",
  "--max-n", 
  "1",
  "-q", 
  "15"
)
```

loop over the list of files, running cutadapt on each one
```{r}
for (i in seq_along(fwd_files)) {

  args <- c(
    fwd_args,
    rev_args,
    cutadapt_extra,
    "-o", fwd_cut[i],
    "-p", rev_cut[i],
    fwd_files[i],
    rev_files[i]
  )

  system2(cutadapt, args = args, stdout = cut_logs[i])
}

# check
head(list.files(cut_dir))
```
